Findings triage (first grade): **HOLD — stays `finding`.**

Why held rather than promoted: the interaction is pinned (`runtime-gate.test.ts`, per the card) so it cannot drift silently; nothing breaks at runtime; and the card itself is honest that none of the three fix shapes is obviously right — the real open question ("which reading wins for a bare RHS word") is precisely what a queued card would have to have answered to be dispatchable. Promoting it now would hand a dev an unscoped decision, not a fix.

Why not `needs-user-decision`: this is diagnostics-UX inside the `spec-tooling` lane, below the escalation bar (no public-contract or product-semantics fork; the #7659 severity split already carries its ruling from objectui#4049 and the card explicitly does not reopen it).

Premise re-checked this round on `origin/main` @ `a3c0865`: both rules exist and fire independently; nothing has landed that reconciles the messages. Re-check trigger for the lane: the next card that touches either rule's message text should reconcile the pair in the same PR (shapes 1-3 on this card are the menu).

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

> Claim: `domain:spec-tooling` seat (#6018) · session `session_01KJATVrh6V2ysutYUJigh3B` · branch `claude/issue-7696-reconcile-bare-word-prescriptions` · round 16 · model `opus` · `mode:cloud`

`pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` as one write, read back. (First claim on this seat using the `Claim:` spelling ruled in #7553 — the previous `**Claimed by …**` form is unreadable to patrol predicate H2.)

## What must be decided, and the default to beat

⚠️ Triage promoted this **without picking** among the card's four options, and the card itself says none is obviously right. So the choice is the dev's — **make it, argue it, and do not silently pick the cheapest.**

**Default to beat: option 2** — one merged finding for this position naming both sanctioned spellings and letting the author choose. Reason it is the default: options 1 and 3 both require settling *which reading wins for a bare word on an RHS*, and that is **the open question itself**, not a step toward answering it. Option 2 delivers a correct message without pretending to know the author's intent.

⛔ **Option 4 (accept as-is) is not available** — it would make this an empty dispatch, and the card was promoted precisely because oscillating prescriptions are direct author harm.

If you deviate, say which reading you concluded wins and on what evidence.

## The facts, restated so this comment stands alone

For `status == active`, two publish-time rules both fire:

| rule | severity | reads it as | prescribes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visibility-bare-identifier` | **`error`** | a dropped binding root | `data.active` |
| `predicate-rhs-path-shaped` | **`warning`** | a literal missing quotes | `'active'` |

Both true about the token, **opposite about the intent**, and the louder one blocks. ⚠️ Note the asymmetry that makes this harmful rather than merely untidy: the bare-word spelling **works today** (objectui#4049 ruled exactly that), so the `error` tells an author to change something that currently renders correctly, in a direction that may break it — and if they comply, the path probably does not resolve and #7214's `predicate-path-unresolved` fires next. A three-corner walk.

The pair is already **pinned in `runtime-gate.test.ts`**, so your reconciliation has a test anchor and the pin must end up asserting the reconciled behaviour rather than the contradiction.

## ⚠️ Serialization — read before you touch the test file

`runtime-gate.test.ts` is a **hot file** in this lane. **#7576** (block-level `surfaces` for `validateSecurityPosture` — 13 rules in one field) is deliberately **held behind this card** and will be dispatched once this lands, because it also rewrites expectations in that file. ⛔ Do not restructure `runtime-gate.test.ts` beyond the region carrying this pair; a broad reformat there will collide.

## Scope

- **In**: `packages/lint/src/validate-predicate-path-refs.ts` (the two rules' messages / emission), the `runtime-gate.test.ts` region pinning the pair, tests, changeset if the behaviour changes.
- ⛔ **Out**: `#7214`'s resolution logic; `authoring-rules.ts` registration; ⛔ `content/docs/releases/**`; the severity **split** landed by #7659 (⛔ do not revisit `error`-on-dotted-chain / `warning`-on-bare-word — that was argued from the family's own bar and is not what this card reopens).
- ㉕ — disclose any expansion rather than absorbing it.

## Accept bar

- **A controls table showing what an author sees for `status == active` before and after** — that is the deliverable's whole point, and prose about it is not evidence.
- The three neighbours stay unchanged: a dotted chain still `error`; a quoted literal still silent; a left-side path still silent. ⛔ If the message tells authors to do X, X must not itself be reported.
- **A scanner must prove it can see before any silence is believed** — pair every silence with a control that fires.
- ⚠️ **`#7484` applies if you touch any doc anchor**: `lychee.toml` sets `include_fragments = "none"`, so a link to a non-existent anchor returns `[200] ✅ OK`. A green link gate is never evidence an anchor resolves.

Counts: `grep -c` / `wc -l`, ⛔ never `grep | head`; reconcile against any in-repo pin.

Report at draft-PR time (#6644 L2) — ⛔ no idle-polling CI; convergence, ready-flip and landing are the PM's. Issue comment carrying the `os-dev-report` marker first, return message second.

> os-dev report · session `session_01VazgUHoW88FzFkGykVzJLM` · branch `claude/issue-7696-reconcile-bare-word-prescriptions` · draft PR #7810 ## Option taken: **2** — one merged finding, both spellings named I took the default rather than beating it, but the argument for it turned out **stronger than the card assumed**, and it did not require answering the open question ("which reading wins for a bare RHS word"). What settles the mechanics is narrower and measurable: > **The rooted reading has no spelling in this position.** `visibility-bare-identifier` told the author to write `data.active` on the right of `==`. That is a dotted chain on the RIGHT — `predicate-rhs-path-shaped`'s own `error` arm. **The same gate refuses the fix it prescribes.** Measured: row 6 of the table below. So standing the rooted prescription down is not choosing a reading; it is deleting a spelling the surface does not have. And the `error`'s own bar — *"there is no reading of the metadata under which it was going to work"* — is **false** at this position, because the literal reading works today (objectui#4049). The surviving advisory names **both** readings and lets the author pick, which is what option 2 asks for. This is option 2 *including* the stand-down that option 2 implies: "a single finding" is not achievable while a second rule keeps emitting a contradictory one. I am not claiming it is option 2 with no cost — the cost is a special case in two rules, exactly as the card priced it. ## Controls table — `status == active` and its neighbours, before and after Measured at the runtime publish gate (`runRuntimeAuthoringRules({ type: 'view', … })`) on `origin/main@098b629` vs the branch. `FORM` = schema-bound metadata form; `RTV` = runtime view. | # | predicate | before | after | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | `FORM data.type == active` | **`error` `visibility-bare-identifier`** → *"write `record.active`"*
`warning` `predicate-rhs-path-shaped` → *"write `'active'`"* | `warning` `predicate-rhs-path-shaped` — **only finding**, names both spellings | | 2 | `FORM data.type == label` (`label` **is** a schema key) | **`error` `visibility-bare-identifier`** → `record.label`
**`error` `predicate-path-unrooted`** → `data.label`
`warning` `predicate-rhs-path-shaped` → `'label'` — **three** prescriptions | `warning` `predicate-rhs-path-shaped` — only finding | | 3 | `FORM status == active` | `error` `visibility-bare-identifier` (on `status`) + `warning` rhs | **unchanged** | | 4 | `FORM data.type == data.label` (dotted chain) | `error` `predicate-rhs-path-shaped` | **unchanged** | | 5 | `FORM data.type == 'active'` (quoted literal) | silent¹ | **unchanged** | | 6 | `FORM data.type == data.active` — *the old error's own prescription* | **`error` `predicate-rhs-path-shaped`** + `error` `predicate-path-unresolved` | **unchanged** — the proof behind row 1 | | 7 | `FORM data.tpye == active` | `error` `visibility-bare-identifier` + `error` `predicate-path-unresolved` | `error` `predicate-path-unresolved` only | | 8 | `RTV record.status == active` | `error` `visibility-bare-identifier` → `record.active` | **unchanged** | | 9 | `RTV record.status == 'active'` | silent | **unchanged** | | 10 | `FORM active == data.type` (bare on the **left**) | `error` `visibility-bare-identifier` | **unchanged** | | 11 | `FORM data.name == active && active` | `error` `visibility-bare-identifier` | **unchanged** | | 12 | `FORM data.tags.all(t, t == active)` (macro body) | `error` `visibility-bare-identifier` | **unchanged** | | 13 | `FORM` unresolvable `schemaId`, `data.x == active` | `error` `visibility-bare-identifier` | `warning` `predicate-rhs-path-shaped` | | 14 | `FORM` unresolvable `schemaId`, `data.x == data.y` | **silent**¹ | `error` `predicate-rhs-path-shaped` | ¹ every `FORM` row also carries a pre-existing `warning visibility-root-mislayered` — unrelated, unchanged, disclosed below. ### Every control and its outcome - **Silence paired with a firing control, per the bar.** Row 1's new silence from `visibility-bare-identifier` is paired with rows 3, 10, 11, 12 — the same rule, the same schema-bound form, still firing. Row 2's silence from `predicate-path-unrooted` is paired with a unit control (`type == 'formula'` → `predicate-path-unrooted`) and `data.name == type && type` → both rules. Row 7 pairs #7214's silence-on-the-right with its firing on the left. - **Accept bar "if your message tells authors to do X, X must not itself be reported":** the new hint's two recommendations are `data.type == 'active'` (row 5, silent) and `data.active == 'yes'` (silent when the field exists). When the field does **not** exist, `predicate-path-unresolved` fires — a *new statement about a different mistake*, not the old ring-around; pinned as its own test. The spelling the hint now warns **against** is row 6, reported at `error` — so the warning is not noise. - **Three neighbours held, as required:** dotted chain still `error` (row 4), quoted literal still silent (row 5), left-side path still silent (row 5 / the `data.type == 'text'` corpus entry). ## What changed - **`packages/lint/src/predicate-rhs-position.ts`** (new) — the shared answer to "which identifiers occur *only* as the bare right operand of `==` / `!=`", plus the shared `schemaIdOf` test for "the metadata-admin evaluator renders this". Shared so the rule that *reports* the position and the rules that *stand down* for it cannot drift about where it applies. - **`validate-predicate-path-refs.ts`** — `predicate-path-unrooted` stands down for that set; the bare arm of `predicate-rhs-path-shaped` carries the merged message; a site whose `schemaId` resolves to nothing is walked with no scope instead of skipped. - **`validate-visibility-predicates.ts`** — `visibility-bare-identifier` stands down for that set, on schema-bound form sites only, fed through the *declared* list (the same conservative mechanism `namespaceRoots` already uses — a name added there can only remove a finding, never invent one). - **`runtime-gate.test.ts`** — the pin now asserts the reconciled behaviour, two tests added beside it, one line added to the property corpus. ⛔ Nothing else in the file is touched, per the **#7576** serialization hold. - Unit tests in both rules' own suites; changeset `predicate-bare-word-rhs-reconciled.md` (`@objectstack/lint: patch`). ## Scope expansions — disclosed, not absorbed (㉕) 1. **`validate-visibility-predicates.ts` was edited**, though scope named only `validate-predicate-path-refs.ts`. Unavoidable: `visibility-bare-identifier` lives there and is the `error` this card is about; option 2's stated cost is "a special case in two rules". 2. **A new file** to hold the one condition both files must agree on. 3. **The walk widening** (row 14) — a coverage *increase*, and what keeps the stand-down from becoming a silence on a form whose `schemaId` this package cannot resolve. ## Found while measuring, NOT fixed — worth its own card At the runtime gate, `validateVisibilityPredicates` runs with `opts.layer` at its `'runtime'` default for **every** view, including schema-bound metadata forms. Two consequences, both pre-existing: - a correctly-`data.`-rooted metadata form draws a `visibility-root-mislayered` advisory telling the author to use `record.` (the ¹ rows); - before this PR the bare-identifier error prescribed **`record.active`**, not the `data.active` this issue's table quotes — the contradiction was real but one notch worse than filed. That is layer plumbing in the gate, not the bare-word pair this card reopened. Left untouched. ## Gates | gate | invocation | result | |---|---|---| | unit tests | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run test` | **70 files, 1921 passed** | | typecheck | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run typecheck` | clean | | eslint | `npx eslint <6 changed files> --no-inline-config` | clean | | changeset gates | `node scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs` / `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` / `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | all ✓ | | real-app corpus | `os build` in `examples/app-showcase`, `examples/app-crm` | `grep -c` over the four rule ids = **0** on both, unchanged | Counts via `grep -c`; no `grep | head` in any counting pipeline. ## Not verified - **CI.** Not run, not polled — the PM's per #6644 L2. - **The renderer end.** objectui's `parseLiteral` behaviour is taken from the in-repo citations (objectui#4049 / PR #4264, and this file's own `PATH_SHAPED_RHS` quoted verbatim from `PATH_SHAPED_LITERAL`). I did not open the objectui checkout to re-read the evaluator. - **`opts.layer: 'metadata'` callers.** `grep` finds that spelling only in this package's tests today, so a `*.form.ts` linted that way but published without a `{ provider: 'schema' }` data source does **not** get the stand-down. That is deliberate (no replacement rule fires there, so standing down would be silence), but it means the reconciliation is keyed on the data source, not on the layer option — if a file-aware caller ever lands, it will need the same key. - **No doc anchors or headings were touched**, so #7484's lychee caveat does not arise here. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_
